sections.h2: What and where is San Miguel County, NM?
sections.html:
San Miguel County is a long, narrow county in northeastern New Mexico that runs from the Great Plains to the Rocky Mountains. Wikipedia gives a 2020 census population of 27,201, names Las Vegas as the county seat, and says the county is more than 100 miles long from east to west and 40 miles wide north to south.

The terrain swings a lot. The highest point is Elk Mountain at 11,661 feet, and the lowest is on the Canadian River at about 3,800 feet. The county covers 4,736 square miles, nearly all of it land.

The same entry says the county was created in 1846 by the United States Army during the Mexican-American War. The Santa Fe Trail, first travelled in 1821, passed through it, and the railroad arrived in 1879, which expanded the market for ranch land and the livestock industry, especially sheep for wool.

sections.h2: What towns and communities make up San Miguel County?
sections.html:
Las Vegas is the only city, and the county also has the villages of Pecos and part of Mosquero. The census-designated places include Conchas Dam, East Pecos, Pueblo, Ribera, Rowe, San Jose, Sena, Tecolote, Tecolotito and Villanueva, and smaller communities include Sapello, Rociada, Montezuma, Ilfeld, San Miguel del Vado and Tererro.

Most of these places are small and spread across a county that is 4,736 square miles. A house in Sapello or Rociada is a long way from the services in Las Vegas, so a seller there should expect a buyer to ask about access, utilities and the property's boundaries before agreeing to a price.

  • City: Las Vegas
  • Villages: Pecos, Mosquero (part)
  • Mountain and valley communities: Sapello, Rociada, Tererro, Montezuma
  • Plains communities: Conchas Dam, Trementina

sections.h2: What does the San Miguel County economy rest on?
sections.html:
Education and public institutions anchor the local economy, and the county's history of ranching and rail still shows. New Mexico Highlands University is listed among the county's higher education institutions on Wikipedia, and United World College, USA occupies the historic Montezuma Castle site northwest of Las Vegas, about 70 miles from Santa Fe, and was founded in 1982.

No official county economic profile with employer counts turned up in our research, so this page makes no claim about the largest employer or job totals. The county entry does say San Miguel County makes up the Las Vegas Micropolitan Statistical Area, which belongs to the larger Albuquerque, Santa Fe and Las Vegas combined statistical area.

sections.h2: Which San Miguel County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Treasurer share an address and work in sequence. The Assessor values property and builds the tax roll, then hands it to the Treasurer in the fall.

Both county offices list weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The Treasurer also takes online payment through a bill-pay site and by phone at 877-690-3729 using Jurisdiction #4115, and asks owners with trouble paying online to call 505-425-9377 so payments are not doubled.

sections.h2: When are San Miguel County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first half is due November 10 and becomes delinquent on December 11, and the second half is due April 10 and becomes delinquent on May 11. The Treasurer's page states these dates for the 2025 tax year and warns that late fees accrue on the 11th of every month on past due balances, even if the owner makes partial payments.

The page also says the State Taxation and Revenue Department auctions property in the third year of delinquency, and that the Treasurer can accept payments toward an account only until the account lands on the state's list.

The Assessor publishes a yearly calendar too. It shows an assessment period from January 1 to February 28, tax rates entered on September 1, the tax roll going to the Treasurer on October 1, and a mass year rollover starting December 1. That calendar lists the Notice of Valuation date as June 1, so read the date printed on your own notice instead of assuming the county's schedule matches another county's.

sections.h2: Is a tax auction scheduled in San Miguel County?
sections.html:
The Taxation and Revenue Department's auction page lists a San Miguel County sale on November 19, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., with a downloadable advertisement and a registration link. It states that registration begins at 8 a.m. and closes at 10 a.m. when the auction starts.

The page says all property is sold as is, with no refunds, and that the minimum bid is based on taxes, penalty, interest and costs. The state issues a tax deed equivalent to a quitclaim deed. A tax sale extinguishes the tax lien only, and no other liens go away.

If your name or a relative's is on the sale list, the sale lists are also available from the County Treasurer or Assessor. New Mexico has no right of redemption, but the page notes a two-year period to challenge the sale in court under Section 7-38-70. That is a narrow remedy, and it is far better to pay the delinquent balance or sell the house before the sale date.

sections.h2: How do I protest a San Miguel County valuation?
sections.html:
File a written protest with the Assessor within the statutory window. Section 7-38-24 NMSA 1978, reprinted in the state's protest pamphlet, requires the petition to be filed by the later of April 1 or thirty days after the notice of valuation is mailed. It must give the owner's name and address, describe the property, and explain why the value is wrong and what the correct one is.

The County Assessor's page offers a 2026 protest petition and a 2026 protest pamphlet in English and Spanish. The Assessor's staff is also conducting reappraisals across the county, and the page says appraisers carry county identification and wear safety vests, so a visit from an appraiser is not unusual.

A county valuation protests board of three decides each protest within 180 days, and a decision can be appealed to district court within thirty days. Residential value growth is also limited to the higher of 103 percent of the prior year or 106.1 percent of two years earlier, except after a change of ownership or new improvements.

sections.h2: What should a San Miguel County seller do about tax due?
sections.html:
A seller should find every unpaid year, confirm the state has not already listed the parcel, and give the title company a payoff figure. Sandoval County's treasurer states that property tax cannot be prorated, so the division of the year between seller and buyer is settled in the sale paperwork; ask the San Miguel County Treasurer how it handles a sale mid-year.

  • Call the Treasurer at 505-425-9376 for the balance on each year.
  • Ask whether the parcel appears on the State's current delinquent list.
  • Check the Assessor's records for the owner of record, especially on inherited land passed through a family without a recorded deed.
  • If the sale includes a mobile home, ask the Assessor whether a tax release is needed.

Cash Home Buyers buys San Miguel County houses as is, including houses with back taxes, unclear title paperwork or repairs the owner cannot fund. We make a written cash offer and the owner decides.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of San Miguel County, NM?
faqs.a: Las Vegas is the county seat. The Treasurer and Assessor both have offices at 500 W. National Ave. in Las Vegas, NM 87701.

faqs.q: When are San Miguel County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and delinquent December 11. The second half is due April 10 and delinquent May 11. Late fees continue to accrue on the 11th of each month on past due balances.

faqs.q: When does San Miguel County property go to tax auction?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page says the state auctions property in the third year of delinquency. The Property Tax Division's page lists a San Miguel County auction on November 19, 2026, at 10:00 a.m.

faqs.q: How do I protest my San Miguel County property value?
faqs.a: File a written petition with the County Assessor by the later of April 1 or thirty days after the notice of valuation is mailed. State why the value is wrong and what you believe is correct.

faqs.q: Does San Miguel County prorate property tax at closing?
faqs.a: Sandoval County's Treasurer says property tax cannot be prorated, so the split between seller and buyer is settled in the sale paperwork. Ask the San Miguel County Treasurer about its own practice; the title company will request the payoff.

faqs.q: Can I sell a San Miguel County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid balance is paid out of the sale proceeds at closing. Selling before the parcel is sold at state auction keeps the owner in control of the outcome.
